text.p: Rentokil Initial Plc chief executive Sir Clive Thompson said on Wednesday that the strong contribution of BET businesses to 1996 results showed that the acquisition was "well under control."
But in a telephone interview with Reuters he said that all parts of the merged business would receive equal attention in 1997.

Shares in the company, formed last year when Rentokil acquired rival BET for 2.1 billion stg, continued to slide in midafternoon trading, falling 36 pence or 7.9 percent to 422 pence, despite full-year pre-tax profits in line with forecasts.
Traders said there was concern that the results had relied too heavily on BET, while Rentokil's core businesses had underperformed.

"I can only assume that analysts were expecting a different shape to the business," Thompson said. "If there was a choice I would much prefer to have a strong performance from BET which indicates that we have them well under control."
Thompson said he had instructed managers to concentrate on integrating the BET operations last year, but added "in 1997 there will no longer be two different businesses. There is one."

He said the group had started talks on selling all the businesses selected for disposal, which include the resorts management operations, but would not "rush in" to agreements in order to achieve the best price.
The company expects to realise between 50 and 100 million stg from disposals in the next 12 months.
